notes.headline: Skydance: first report after swallowing Warner Bros. Discovery shows Paramount+ revenue up 21% and a $6 billion savings target
notes.takeaway: In its last quarter before the Warner Bros. Discovery deal closed, Paramount Skydance grew revenue 5% to $7.0 billion and earned $1.0 billion of adjusted EBITDA, with Paramount+ revenue up 21%. Adjusted EPS of $0.45 was well above the $0.20 consensus. The combined Skydance targets at least $6 billion of annual synergies and will bundle HBO Max with Paramount+ in early 2027.
results: Paramount Skydance, excluding Warner Bros. Discovery, reported revenue of $7.0 billion for the third quarter, up 5%, net earnings of $73 million and adjusted EBITDA of $1.0 billion, a 14% margin. It said it remains on track for the high end of its 2026 profit outlook of $3.9 billion of adjusted EBITDA. Adjusted EPS was $0.45 against analysts’ $0.20.

Paramount+ revenue grew 21%, its fastest growth this year, with revenue per user up about 14%. Studio revenue rose 23% and the TV Media division, which includes CBS and the cable networks, achieved a 34% adjusted EBITDA margin. On a pro forma basis including Warner Bros. Discovery, direct-to-consumer revenue grew 15%.

The acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery closed on October 6, 2026. Paramount+, HBO and HBO Max together reach 203 million subscribers in more than 130 markets, and Pluto TV has about 75 million monthly users; on Nielsen data the combined group is the second-largest distributor of US TV viewing after YouTube.
mgmt: Chairman and chief executive David Ellison and co-chief executive Ynon Kreiz wrote that the combined company aims to be the premier global content engine, accelerate an integrated streaming platform and build the next-generation media company powered by creativity and technology. They target at least $6 billion of annual run-rate synergies within three years, with more than 20 workstreams under way, and plan to cut net leverage to 3.0 times by the end of 2029 and reach investment-grade credit metrics.

For the fourth quarter they expect continued strong streaming growth and TV trends consistent with recent quarters, but said the improved Paramount film slate will be more than offset by the underperformance of the Warner Bros. film slate.
view: This is the most consequential media merger since Disney bought Fox. David Ellison, backed by his father Larry Ellison’s fortune, bought Paramount in 2025 and has now absorbed Warner Bros. Discovery, uniting CBS, Paramount Pictures, Nickelodeon, MTV, CNN, HBO, Warner Bros., DC and Discovery under one roof. The strategic logic is scale in streaming: Paramount+ alone was too small to compete with Netflix and Disney, and HBO Max had the prestige content but not the reach. A combined service of more than 200 million subscribers is large enough to matter.

The standalone Paramount numbers are better than many expected. Paramount+ revenue growing 21% with prices rising 14% shows the service has pricing power, and a 34% margin in traditional TV shows that the declining cable business still throws off a lot of cash to fund the transition. That cash is essential, because the combined company carries a very large debt load from the acquisition — hence the target of reaching 3.0 times leverage only by 2029.

The risks are classic merger risks magnified. Delivering $6 billion of savings means deep cuts across overlapping networks, studios and back offices, at a time when the industry is already shrinking. The Warner Bros. film slate is already flagged as a fourth-quarter drag, and integrating two companies with very different cultures under a new owner is hard. The very low share price reflects heavy dilution from the deal and scepticism about the debt; the first combined quarter in early 2027 will show whether the synergy plan is real.
notes.watch: Watch the first combined results, progress on the $6 billion synergy target, the HBO Max and Paramount+ bundle launch in early 2027, debt reduction, and any sale of cable networks.
